notes.text: Both alternatives retain sociological theory and empirical social-research methods. VU additionally teaches dedicated inequality specialisms, social-network analysis, co-creative enquiry, intervention evaluation and an individual 18 EC thesis. Technical programming, general psychology and organisational leadership do not supply these missing specialist components.

VU integrates four compulsory projects around policy advice, commissioned research, social entrepreneurship and consultancy with societal partners. UCR community work, economics and communication provide different applied experiences; they do not reproduce that sequence. Optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Sociology examines diversity, inequality and communication and technology through sociological theory and qualitative and quantitative research. Students work with societal partners in four professional project roles, then undertake intervention evaluation and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two qualified UCR alternatives combine a substantive sociology and social-research core with broader social-science perspectives or digital methods and media analysis. Specialist inequality, network analysis, co-creative methods, integrated project practice and thesis requirements remain different.

curriculum.limitation: This 180 EC illustration selects Beyond Gender Inequalities and AI & Society from two restricted menus and preserves 30 EC of approved open study. Language testing or a refresher gates Project 1; mentoring has no additional credit. Attendance, prior-course participation or passes, open-study approval and thesis-entry requirements apply. The thesis requires 90 EC from Years 1–2 and participation in intervention evaluation.
